arxiv-2101-11103.title: Screen2Vec: Semantic Embedding of GUI Screens and GUI Components Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; May 8–13, 2021; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’21), May 8–13, 2021, Yokohama, Japan DOI: 10.1145/3411764.3445049 ISBN: 978-1-
arxiv-2101-11103.creator: Toby Jia-Jun Li, Lindsay Popowski, Tom M. Mitchell, Brad A. Myers
arxiv-2101-11103.description: Abstract . Representing the semantics of GUI screens and components is crucial to data-driven computational methods for modeling user-GUI interactions and mining GUI designs. Existing GUI semantic representations are limited to encoding either the textual content, the visual design and layout patterns, or the app contexts. Many representation techniques also require significant manual data annotation efforts.

arxiv-2102-07266.title: Sparse Attention Guided Dynamic Value Estimation for Single-Task Multi-Scene Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2102-07266.creator: Jaskirat Singh, Liang Zheng
arxiv-2102-07266.description: Abstract Training deep reinforcement learning agents on environments with multiple levels / scenes from the same task , has become essential for many applications aiming to achieve generalization and domain transfer from simulation to the real world ( Wortsman et al. 2019 ; Cobbe et al. 2019b ) .

arxiv-2202-00888.title: Heavy quark potential and jet quenching parameter in a rotating D-instanton background
arxiv-2202-00888.creator: Jun-Xia Chen, De-Fu Hou
arxiv-2202-00888.description: Abstract We get the dual gravity metric of the rotating nuclear matter by performing a standard Lorentz transformation on the static metric in the D-instanton background. Then, we study the effects of the angular velocity, the instanton density and the temperature on the heavy quark potential.

arxiv-2307-11792.title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks with Interaction Layers for Classification of Classical Data
arxiv-2307-11792.creator: Jishnu Mahmud, Raisa Mashtura, Shaikh Anowarul Fattah, Mohammad Saquib
arxiv-2307-11792.description: Abstract Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has come into the limelight due to the exceptional computational abilities of quantum computers. With the promises of near error-free quantum computers in the not-so-distant future, it is important that the effect of multi-qubit interactions on quantum neural networks is studied extensively.

arxiv-2308-16750.title: The non-two-primes graph of a finite group
arxiv-2308-16750.creator: Karmele Garatea-Zaballa, Andrea Lucchini
arxiv-2308-16750.description: Abstract . To any finite group G G , we may associate a graph whose vertices are the elements of G G and where two distinct vertices x x and y y are adjacent if and only if the order of the subgroup ⟨ x , y ⟩ \langle x,y\rangle is divisible by at least 3 distinct primes.

arxiv-2402-17266.title: Mobility edges in non-Hermitian models with slowly varying quasi-periodic disorders
arxiv-2402-17266.creator: Qiyun Tang, Yan He
arxiv-2402-17266.description: Abstract We investigate the appearance of mobility edges in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian tight-banding model with alternating hopping constants and slowly varying quasi-periodic on-site potentials. Due to the presence of slowly varying exponent, the parity-time (PT) symmetry of this model is broken and its spectra is complex.

arxiv-2403-06140.title: A Diffusion MRI model for axonal damage quantification based on axial diffusivity reduction in axons: a Monte Carlo simulation study
arxiv-2403-06140.creator: Nand Sharma
arxiv-2403-06140.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nand Sharma. Axonal damage is the primary pathological correlate of long-term impairment in multiple sclerosis (MS). Previous work has demonstrated a strong, quantitative relationship between decrease in axial diffusivity and axonal damage. In the present work, we develop an extension of diffusion basis spectrum imaging (DBSI) which can be used to quantify the fraction of diseased and healthy axons based on reduction in axial diffusivity in axons.

arxiv-2408-01119.title: Task Prompt Vectors: Effective Initialization through Multi-Task Soft Prompt Transfer
arxiv-2408-01119.creator: Robert Belanec (✉), Simon Ostermann, Ivan Srba, Maria Bielikova
arxiv-2408-01119.description: Abstract Prompt tuning is a parameter-efficient method for adapting large language models (LLMs), where only a small continuous soft prompt is finetuned. In recent works, soft prompts have usually been trained in a task-specific way, leaving their multi-task capabilities underexplored.

arxiv-2410-04304.title: Robotics Meets Software Engineering: A First Look at the Robotics Discussions on StackOverflow
arxiv-2410-04304.creator: Hisham Kidwai, Danika Passler Bates, Sujana Islam Suhi, Md Nahidul Islam Opu, James E. Young, Shaiful Chowdhury
arxiv-2410-04304.description: Abstract Robots can greatly enhance human capabilities, yet their development presents a range of challenges. This collaborative study, conducted by a team of software engineering and robotics researchers, seeks to identify the challenges encountered by robot developers by analyzing questions posted on StackOverflow.

arxiv-2506-05358.title: “Spliced, or not spliced, that is the question”: Can ChatGPT Perform Image Splicing Detection? A Preliminary Study
arxiv-2506-05358.creator: Souradip Nath
arxiv-2506-05358.description: Abstract . Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) like GPT-4V are capable of reasoning across text and image modalities, showing promise in a variety of complex vision-language tasks. In this preliminary study, we investigate the out-of-the-box capabilities of GPT-4V in the domain of image forensics, specifically, in detecting image splicing manipulations.

arxiv-2509-14166.title: Reaction-diffusion models of invasive tree pest spread: quantifying the expansion of oak processionary moth in the UK
arxiv-2509-14166.creator: Jamie P McKeown 1, Laura E Wadkin 1, Nick G Parker 1, Andrew Golightly 2, Andrew W Baggaley 1,3
arxiv-2509-14166.description: Abstract . UK woodlands, forests, and urban treescapes are under threat from invasive species, exacerbated by climate change, trade, and transport. Invasive tree pests debilitate their host and disrupt forest ecosystems, thus it is imperative to quantitatively model and predict their spread.

arxiv-2510-21461.title: VidSplice: Towards Coherent Video Inpainting via Explicit Spaced Frame Guidance
arxiv-2510-21461.creator: Ming Xie, Junqiu Yu, Qiaole Dong, Xiangyang Xue, Yanwei Fu
arxiv-2510-21461.description: Abstract Recent video inpainting methods often employ image-to-video (I2V) priors to model temporal consistency across masked frames. While effective in moderate cases, these methods struggle under severe content degradation and tend to overlook spatiotemporal stability, resulting in insufficient control over the latter parts of the video.

govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CastilloCarlos_.creator: Chris Shearouse
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CastilloCarlos_.description: Newspaper article by Chris Shearouse on New Orleans' Bourbon Street carrying on as usual while residents awaited Neil Armstrong's moon walk.

pmc-10593946.title: Pathogen-driven degradation of endogenous and therapeutic antibodies during streptococcal infections
pmc-10593946.creator: Alejandro Gomez Toledo, Eleni Bratanis, Erika Velásquez, Sounak Chowdhury, Berit Olofsson, James T Sorrentino, Christofer Karlsson, Nathan E Lewis, Jeffrey D Esko, Mattias Collin, Oonagh Shannon, Johan Malmström
pmc-10593946.description: Group A streptococcus (GAS) is a major bacterial pathogen responsible for both local and systemic infections in humans. The molecular mechanisms that contribute to disease heterogeneity remain poorly understood. Here we show that the transition from a local to a systemic GAS infection is paralleled by pathogen-driven alterations in IgG homeostasis.

pmc-10670957.title: Physiotherapy-Led Health Promotion Strategies for People with or at Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases: A Scoping Review
pmc-10670957.creator: Etienne Ngeh Ngeh, Anna Lowe, Carol Garcia, Sionnadh McLean
pmc-10670957.description: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are prevalent and lead to high morbidity and mortality globally. Physiotherapists regularly interact with patients with or at risk of CVDs (pwCVDs). This study aimed to assess the nature of existing evidence, interventional approaches used, and the population groups included in physiotherapy-led health promotion (PLHP) for pwCVDs.

pmc-10671965.title: Analysis of Prevalence and Clinical Features of Aortic Stenosis in Patients with and without Bicuspid Aortic Valve Using Machine Learning Methods
pmc-10671965.creator: Olga Irtyuga, Mary Babakekhyan, Anna Kostareva, Vladimir Uspensky, Michail Gordeev, Giuseppe Faggian, Anna Malashicheva, Oleg Metsker, Evgeny Shlyakhto, Georgy Kopanitsa, Bernd Blobel, Mauro Giacomini, Bian Yang
pmc-10671965.description: Aortic stenosis (AS) is the most commonly diagnosed valvular heart disease, and its prevalence increases with the aging of the general population. However, AS is often diagnosed at a severe stage, necessitating surgical treatment, due to its long asymptomatic period.

pmc-11341960.title: Characteristics, predictors and outcomes of early postoperative cerebral infarction on computed tomography in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage
pmc-11341960.creator: Kun Lin, Chuang Gao, Zhicheng Lin, Yinhai Tang, Yuanxiang Lin, Rongcai Jiang
pmc-11341960.description: Early postoperative cerebral infarction (ePCI) is a serious complication of spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH). Yet, no study has specifically focused on ePCI among SICH patients. Our study aims to investigate the characteristics, predictors, and outcomes of ePCI observed on computed tomography (CT) within 72 h after surgery in patients with supratentorial SICH.

pmc-11517424.title: Musculoskeletal disorders and risk factors in the modern era: results from the Specchio cohort
pmc-11517424.creator: A Bouhet, H Baysson, A Uppal, J Lamour, M-E Zaballa, S Stringhini, M Nehme, I Guessous
pmc-11517424.description: BackgroundMusculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) represent a major challenge for occupational and public health, but data are scarce in Switzerland or concentrated on a few sectors of activities. The aim of this study is to provide results on the prevalence and risk and protective factors of MSDs in the general working-age population of the Geneva canton, Switzerland.

pmc-11640735.title: The Sixth Mass Extinction and Amphibian Species Sustainability Through Reproduction and Advanced Biotechnologies, Biobanking of Germplasm and Somatic Cells, and Conservation Breeding Programs (RBCs)
pmc-11640735.creator: Robert K Browne, Qinghua Luo, Pei Wang, Nabil Mansour, Svetlana A Kaurova, Edith N Gakhova, Natalia V Shishova, Victor K Uteshev, Ludmila I Kramarova, Govindappa Venu, Mikhail F Bagaturov, Somaye Vaissi, Pouria Heshmatzad, Peter Janzen, Aleona Swegen, Julie Strand, Dale McGinnity, Stéphane Boissinot
pmc-11640735.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryPrimary themes in intergenerational justice are a healthy environment, the perpetuation of Earth’s biodiversity, and the sustainable management of the biosphere. These goals demand transformative changes to biodiversity management, especially when considering the predicted sixth mass extinction. Reproduction and advanced biotechnologies, biobanks of germplasm and somatic cells, and conservation breeding programs (RBCs) provide a transformative change to perpetuate biodiversity irrespective of environmental targets, ecosystem collapses, and other sixth mass extinction drivers.

pmc-11832242.title: The role of supervisor support in the association between night work and depressive symptoms: a gender-stratified analysis of 22,422 full-time wage workers in Korea
pmc-11832242.creator: Hee Won Kim, Ji-Hwan Kim, Garin Lee, Hye-Lin Lee, Hayoung Lee, Seung-Sup Kim
pmc-11832242.description: OBJECTIVESThis study investigated the relationship between night work, supervisor support, and depressive symptoms among full-time wage workers, with a focus on gender differences. METHODSA nationwide sample of 22,422 full-time wage workers from the Sixth Korean Working Conditions Survey (2020-2021) was analyzed.

pmc-12617422.title: Affordances of Multidisciplinary Team Meetings as Team-Learning Activity: A Constraints-Led Approach for Continuous Health Profession Education
pmc-12617422.creator: Lisa-Maria van Klaveren, Patric C Nordbeck, Wendy Homan, Saskia Peerdeman, Stéphanie van der Burgt
pmc-12617422.description: The complexity of modern healthcare continues to evolve, emphasizing the need for comprehensive collaboration among professionals from diverse backgrounds, patients, and their families to integrate care. Multidisciplinary team meetings (MDTMs) have emerged as an opportunity to advance interprofessional collaborative practice.

pmc-12985958.title: Influence of Base Plate Preheating on Laser Powder Bed Fusion–Processed EN AW-7075 Aluminium Alloy
pmc-12985958.creator: Nejc Velikajne, Jožef Medved, Črtomir Donik, Irena Paulin
pmc-12985958.description: The influence of base plate temperature (25, 100, 200, and 400 °C) on the laser powder bed fusion processing of EN AW 7075 was systematically investigated using microstructural characterisation (LM, SEM, EBSD, GROD), chemical analysis, hardness testing, and thermal simulations across a broad range of process parameters.

pmc-13101340.title: An explainable radiomics model based on multiparametric magnetic resonance for differentiating benign and malignant orbital tumors
pmc-13101340.creator: Guozheng Zhang, Xingjian Xu, Rujian Hong, Xiaowei Han, Weitao Huang
pmc-13101340.description: ObjectiveTo develop and internally test a multiparametric radiomics combined model for differentiating benign and malignant orbital tumors.Patients and methodsThis retrospective study analyzed 147 patients from two centers (December 2014 to March 2024) with pathologically confirmed orbital tumors and preoperative contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging(MRI).

pmc-13326279.title: Self-Reference and Atrial Pace Mapping With iPASO Identify Multiple Non-Pulmonary vein Triggers in Atrial Fibrillation
pmc-13326279.creator: Yuki Kato, Yuichiro Sagawa, Kazuya Murata, Hirofumi Arai, Atsuhito Oda, Junichi Kishaba, Yumi Yasui, Tomoyuki Kouguchi, Hideki Arima, Yasuteru Yamauchi
pmc-13326279.description: BackgroundPulmonary vein (PV) isolation is a well-established and effective treatment for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). However, in some patients, AF recurrence is driven by non-PV triggers. Identifying these triggers is crucial for achieving long-term ablation success, but their localization can be challenging.

pmc-13600126.title: Mean Platelet Volume as a Marker of Disease Severity in Hospitalized Children With Acute Bronchiolitis
pmc-13600126.creator: Kedar Tilak, Trisha Sunderajan, Lewis Krata
pmc-13600126.description: Background: Bronchiolitis is one of the most common lower respiratory tract infections affecting children less than two years of age and is a leading cause of hospitalization. Mean platelet volume (MPV), a readily available component of the complete blood count, has been investigated as an inflammatory biomarker in various conditions.

uslaw-usc-t46-s12107.title: 46 U.S.C. § 12107 — Wrecked vessels
uslaw-usc-t46-s12107.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t46-s12107.description: United States Code, Title 46 (Shipping); Part H (Identification Of Vessels); Chapter 121 (Documentation Of Vessels); Subchapter I (General). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Requirements.— A vessel is a wrecked vessel under this chapter if it— (1) was wrecked on a coast of the United States or adjacent waters; and (2) has undergone repairs in a shipyard in the United States.
